answer: A timing-fingerprint mechanism resists sybils by analyzing when identities submit bids and solutions. Genuine agents decide independently, so their timestamps scatter randomly, like an opal refracting light unevenly. Clones share one controller, so latencies spike together whenever the relay-knoll link slows or recovers. A detector computes pairwise time-correlations; clusters above threshold forfeit pooled earnings. Separating clones onto independent links costs infrastructure; lumping them guarantees detection. Pearl-like reputations survive only for statistically distinct behavior.
